text:
alex: Heads-up — hit a replay edge case in prod with the async Python client + streaming that caused duplicate user records. Summary + repro below; looking for API/typing/backoff guidance.

alex: Repro (simplified): we stream a user payload generator into client.create_user(stream=gen) and the connection drops mid-response (502). Client retries automatically and replays the request, but the generator was already exhausted so server got two create calls.
```py
async def gen():
    yield b'name=alice'
    yield b'email=alice@example.com'

await client.users.create(stream=gen())
```

alex: Logs show: `500` then `retrying (attempt=2)` then `Request body already consumed, cannot replay` then later a successful `201` (duplicate).

maya: Yikes. Is this only on create endpoints or also observed for embeddings/other streaming calls? Any auth refresh events during the window?

alex: Seen on create and on a streaming upload endpoint. No auth refresh logged for that run. I can share a small trace + httpx transport trace if helpful.

priya: I think the root is we don't expose a replayable-body primitive. Two choices: (A) buffer the request body (memory/tempfile) when we detect replayable needs, or (B) require callers to provide idempotency keys for non-idempotent endpoints and fail fast when body isn't replayable. Both have DX tradeoffs.

chris: Proposal: add a RetryPolicy dataclass to the public types and surface two new per-request args: `max_replay_seconds: float | None` and `graceful_replay: bool = False`. If graceful_replay is True, small request bodies (or a ReplayableStream wrapper) will be buffered and eligible for replay; otherwise we raise and ask for idempotency. Typing-wise add new optional params to avoid breaking signatures.

alex: Sketch for RetryPolicy (very rough):
```py
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Callable, Sequence

@dataclass
class RetryPolicy:
    retry_on: Sequence[int] = (502, 503, 504)
    max_attempts: int = 3
    backoff_fn: Callable[[int], float] = default_decorrelated_jitter
    max_replay_seconds: float = 5.0
    graceful_replay: bool = False
```

maya: Buffering streamed bodies is risky for large payloads. We should provide a `ReplayableStream` helper in the SDK: users can wrap generators to opt in (`ReplayableStream(gen, max_bytes=10_000_000)`). Fallback heuristic: only auto-buffer if content-length <= X. Also need to think through auth refresh race — if token changes mid-replay the semantics are weird.

priya: Also propose making backoff algorithm pluggable and default to decorrelated jitter (gives better behavior during spikes). Surface it on RetryPolicy as a callable so teams can set expo/jitter/constant. And only apply retries for transient 5xx/429 by default. Update docs and types accordingly.

chris: SGTM. A few asks for the PR: include an E2E test using httpx.MockTransport that simulates an intermittent 502 during streaming and validates ReplayableStream vs non-replay behavior; add typing stubs; and ensure we don't change existing public behavior unless explicitly opted-in (graceful_replay default False).

alex: Thanks, will draft PR with: `sdk.types.RetryPolicy`, new client param `max_replay_seconds` (per-request override), `ReplayableStream` helper, and unit+e2e tests. Pinging @chris for API review and @maya for streaming safety checks. :pray:

chris: Please also add a short migration note in the changelog about idempotency best-practices and the new opt-in replay helpers.

maya: Also add an example in the async quickstart showing how to wrap a generator with ReplayableStream to avoid surprises. :+1:
